category_title: Students overwhelmed by rote volume who require hands-on instructional methods
minimal_context: Zachary is sitting with his tutor to complete a daily first-grade math homework page containing thirty problems.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's open your math book for tonight. You need to complete this page of thirty problems.

STUDENT: That's thirty problems on one page. I can't do a whole page a day.

TUTOR: Just start with the first one and keep going.

STUDENT: It's too many. My brain functions differently than a lot of other children.

TUTOR: You are not really trying to do your math right now. You just need to finish the page.

STUDENT: (Starts to cry) I am just so overwhelmed with that!

options.A: Talk with his parents about his progress on the math homework and frequently discuss his performance during tutoring sessions.
options.B: Meet with a behavior coordinator before and after each session to review goals and trade points for incentives.
options.C: Use hands-on instructional methods and provide individual consideration of his cultural background during the math tutoring sessions.
options.D: Provide access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation by giving him a squishy stress-relief ball.
